questions.q: By how much did DART shorten Dimorphos's lap around Didymos?
questions.do: Read Lap shortened by in the Re-measuring the push card.
questions.a: About 33.2 minutes: from 11 h 55 min 17 s to 11 h 22 min 3 s.

questions.q: With the starting settings, how many DART-class impactors are needed to save Earth?
questions.do: In Defend Earth, keep diameter 151 m, 10 years, β 3.6 and density 2,400 kg/m³. Raise Number of DART-class impactors one step at a time and watch the verdict.
questions.a: 4. With 1 it Still hits (shift 2,986 km, 34% of what is needed). With 3 it is only Grazing (8,958 km against 8,710 km needed). With 4 it is Deflected (11,944 km).

questions.q: With one impactor, what does extra warning time do?
questions.do: Keep 1 impactor. Set Warning time before impact to 1 year and read Shift by impact day. Then slide it to 30 years.
questions.a: 1 year: about 299 km, only 3% of what is needed. 30 years: about 8,958 km, and the verdict becomes Grazing. The shift is 3 × push × time, so 30 times the warning gives 30 times the shift.

questions.q: Why did Dimorphos lose more momentum than DART brought to it?
questions.do: Compare Momentum DART brought with Momentum Dimorphos lost in Re-measuring the push, and read the note below.
questions.a: DART brought about 3,818 kN·s, but Dimorphos lost about 11,758 kN·s, so β is about 3.1. The extra came from the recoil of rock blasted into space by the impact, like the kick of a gun.

questions.q: When did DART hit Dimorphos, and why was it a first in history?
questions.do: Read the introduction at the top of the page.
questions.a: On 26 September 2022 a 610 kg spacecraft hit the 151 m moonlet Dimorphos at 22,530 km/h. It was the first time people deliberately moved a natural object in space. Nothing was threatening Earth; it was a test.
